basic_details.job_title: DCPU Rohtas Support Person Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online for 30 Posts
basic_details.short_information: The District Child Protection Unit (Zila Bal Sanrakshan Ikai), Collectorate, Rohtas, Sasaram, is inviting applications to empanel 30 Support Persons (Sahayak Vyakti) and prepare a waiting list under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 and the POCSO Rules, 2020. Eligible residents of Rohtas district must send the application, mentioning the post applied for, to [email protected] by 24 December 2026, 23:59 hrs; applications received after that date will not be considered.

content_sections.heading: About DCPU Rohtas Support Persons
content_sections.text: The District Child Protection Unit, Rohtas works under the Collectorate, Rohtas at Sasaram, Bihar. This empanelment follows the "Guidelines for Support Persons 2026" issued by the Secretary, Social Welfare Department, Bihar, Patna (guideline memo no. 748 and letter no. 749, both dated 24.04.2026), which are based on the Model Guidelines of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) under Section 39 of the POCSO Act, 2012. A Support Person gives a child victim of a POCSO case emotional and psychological support from before the judicial process starts until it ends, helps the child deal with the legal system and testify, and helps secure rehabilitation, safety and protection. Cases are assigned by the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) from the list of empanelled Support Persons.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: The prescribed application form asks for: Name, father's/husband's name, category (General/Backward/Extremely Backward/SC/ST), caste and gender (male, female, transgender) Date of birth and age as on 01.11.2026 (years, months, days) Nationality, home district, present/correspondence address and permanent address Educational qualification from Matric (10th) to Intermediate, Graduation, Post Graduation, Ph.D. and others, with institution, board/university, year, full marks, marks obtained and division Experience details: institution/office, post, from and to dates, whether currently working, total period A self-attested passport-size colour photograph pasted on the form, and a signed declaration that all information is true

content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: All 30 vacancies are for the post of Support Person in Rohtas district. The category-wise break-up is as printed in the notice: In addition, 20% of the total vacancies fixed for each category will form a waiting list. A Support Person from the waiting list may be engaged only when cases increase, when an empanelled Support Person leaves the work, or in an unavoidable situation. Post Graduation in Social Work (MSW)/Sociology/Psychology/Child Development or Law OR Graduation degree in any faculty with a Diploma in Child Rights/Counselling, along with three years' experience Desirable: at least three years' work experience in child rights/child protection/legal work/social work/child psychology counsellor/sociology/psychology. Preference will be given to experience in the District Legal Services Authority, Bihar State Legal Services Authority, District Child Protection Unit, Child Welfare Committee, Juvenile Justice Board, POCSO Court or Childline/Child Helpline services. Minimum 30 years and maximum 65 years, which the notice describes as the age prescribed in the State for selection of a Child Welfare Committee member. Age will be calculated as on 01.11.2026. Must be a citizen of India. Must be a resident of Rohtas district. Past record must be clean: no criminal case registered anywhere in India, and never convicted of moral turpitude. An affidavit to this effect must be submitted. Must not have been expelled or blacklisted by any institution working in child protection or child development. Remuneration is a maximum of Rs. 9000/- per case, paid in three instalments, per POCSO case. On the request of the Child Welfare Committee and by order of the District Magistrate, a Support Person may be attached to a maximum of 15 cases, provided justice is not affected. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of the post.

content_sections.heading: DCPU Rohtas Support Persons Job Description
content_sections.text: The guidelines list these duties, among others, for a Support Person: Inform the victim and guardian about the Support Person's services and available emergency services. Prepare the child psychologically for the statement, investigation and trial. Inform them of entitlements, services and the progress of the case at each stage. Help apply for compensation/relief under the Bihar Victim Compensation Scheme, the SC/ST Act and other means. Familiarise the child with the Special Court/Juvenile Justice Board and stay with the child during investigation, inquiry, trial and medical examination. Coordinate through DCPU for a counsellor, interpreter or special educator, and with the DLSA for free legal aid. Coordinate with the police station for the victim's safety, and help under the witness protection scheme. Visit the child's home regularly, and report a hostile witness in the monthly report to the CWC and the court. Remain impartial and child-friendly, and protect the victim's privacy and the confidentiality of the case. Before starting work, a Support Person must declare having no dispute or conflict with the victim or any other stakeholder; if the declaration later proves false, the person may be removed and a case may be filed.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Self-attested copies of all educational qualification certificates Mark sheets Experience certificates Caste certificate Character certificate Residential certificate Affidavit on clean past record (as required by the eligibility conditions)

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Candidates will be selected on the basis of educational qualification and an interview by the Selection Committee. The DCPU will scrutinise applications and shortlist eligible candidates; if applications are very many, ten times the vacancies, category-wise, will be called for the personal interview. The Selection Committee is chaired by the senior-most Additional District and Sessions Judge (Special Court POCSO). Its members are the Secretary, District Legal Services Authority; the District Magistrate or a nominee not below Additional District Magistrate; the Head of the Psychology/Sociology faculty of a government college or a subject expert nominated by the District Magistrate; and the Assistant Director, DCPU, as Member-Secretary. The committee will recommend a panel and a waiting list, which will be published on the district's official website and the office notice board. A criminal character verification certificate will be obtained from empanelled Support Persons after publication.

faq.question: Q1. How many Support Person vacancies are there in DCPU Rohtas Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 30 vacancies: SC/ST 08, BC/EBC 06, Minority 06 and Unreserved 10, with a 20% waiting list for each category.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: Applications must be emailed by 24 December 2026, till 23:59 hrs; applications received after that will not be considered.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for a Support Person?
faq.answer: Post Graduation in Social Work (MSW)/Sociology/Psychology/Child Development or Law, or Graduation in any faculty with a Diploma in Child Rights/Counselling along with three years' experience.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: Minimum 30 years and maximum 65 years, calculated as on 01.11.2026.

faq.question: Q5. What is the pay of a Support Person?
faq.answer: A maximum of Rs. 9000/- per case, paid in three instalments, per POCSO case.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply?
faq.answer: Fill the prescribed form from https://rohtas.nic.in, mention the post applied for, attach self-attested certificates and email it to [email protected].

faq.question: Q7. How will candidates be selected?
faq.answer: Through marks for educational qualification (80) and an interview by the Selection Committee (maximum 20 marks).

faq.question: Q8. Who can apply?
faq.answer: Indian citizens who are residents of Rohtas district, have a clean record and have not been expelled or blacklisted by a child protection or child development institution.

faq.question: Q9. Is this a permanent job?
faq.answer: No, Support Persons will be empanelled for 02 years, with an annual review of their work by the Selection Committee.

faq.question: Q10. What must be brought on the interview date?
faq.answer: The originals of all certificates enclosed with the application are compulsory on the interview date.
